short: Allied leaders met in Crimea to discuss the post-war reorganization of Germany and Europe.
full:
Between 4 and 11 February 1945, Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin met at the Yalta Conference in the Crimea. With the defeat of Germany appearing imminent, discussions focused on shaping the post-war peace. The leaders agreed to divide Germany and Berlin into four occupation zones and to demilitarize and denazify the country. Stalin also formally agreed to enter the war against Japan within three months of Germany's surrender.

Yalta became highly controversial in the ensuing Cold War. Although Stalin promised free elections in Poland and other Eastern European nations, the physical occupation of those territories by the Red Army allowed him to establish Soviet-aligned communist governments. The conference effectively laid the groundwork for the geopolitical division of Europe that would last for decades.
